Performance evaluation of the linerboard paper machine for integrating the RF and US- Second scenario The performance evaluation of the corrugated (fluting) medium paper machine for integrating the RF and US within the main and after hoods and air dryer of the dryer section was evaluated. Two scenarios for the above case study demonstrated the capability of the techno-economic model and proposed approach to the solution. The first scenario was carried out by obtaining the actual 49 DE-EE0009395 corrugated (fluting) medium paper machine data from the detailed analysis of open sources [Ghodbanan, et al., 2017: Ghodbanan et al., 2015: 1474-1490; Ghodbanan, et al., 2016], using four RF and US experimental formulations developed in this project to assess the energy intensity reduction and improvement in drying rate relative to the paper moisture content. The RF was applied with a power of 800 W, while the US was used at averaged frequencies of 28, 40, 80, and 120 kHz for the first scenario. The RF was applied with a power of 500 W and only 120 kHz for the second scenario. Tables 10 and 11 show the percentage reduction in energy intensity, the increase in drying and production rates, and the increase in reel speed for each steam cylinder group and the entire dryer section. The steam cylinders in groups 1 and 2 were proposed to be replaced with the RF technology, while the US technology was proposed to be added within the dryer pocket of steam group 3. Therefore, the assessment of the overall performance improvement in the dryer section, including each subsection’s contribution, shows a significant increase in drying and production rates that lines up with project metrics. The percentage reduction in energy intensity reasonably matches the project targets. The increase in reel speed also falls within the allowable industrial range obtained from open sources for several paper mill machine manufacturing companies. Table 10.
